meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Estado Español; unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state incorporation or tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system; Autonomous Communities exercise devolved administrative powers but corporate-law and AML/CFT frameworks are exclusively national)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU, 2009) — freedom of establishment under Article 49
Spain–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1990, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 (transposition of AMLD5) and Real Decreto-ley 10/2022 (UBO-register access); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 1750/2022, de 27 de diciembre (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales — RCTR); Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo (financial-services AML duties context); consistent with Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 and supported by Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (beneficial-ownership single access point).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_detail: The RCTR (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales / BO-SAR) is freely accessible to Spanish and foreign competent authorities and to obliged entities performing customer due diligence; the public, including journalists and civil-society organizations, may access only upon demonstration of legitimate interest. Nominee concealment is not recognized for UBO purposes; any nominee or intermediary must be pierced.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_criteria: Identification of every natural person who, directly or indirectly, owns or exercises control through more than 25% of share capital or voting rights, or who controls the corporate entity by other means (Art. 4 L 10/2010); where no such person is identified after exhausting two successive levels of analysis, control by other means, including senior-management override, must be declared and independently risk-assessed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Vigencia) of each ultimate foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign parent (e.g., Companies House of the UK, registries of Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Panama, or Brazil)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) followed by sworn translation (traducción jurada) into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the ultimate parent authorizing incorporation of the Spanish S.L., the capital contribution schedule, and appointment of initial director(s) and attorney(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states) with sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder para la constitución de la sociedad) granted to the designated Spanish notary or incorporation agent, with express capacities for name reservation, deed execution, and registry filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country in which the grantor/UBO resides, or competent Spanish Consulate where executed consularly
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions); signature legalized before notary in the state of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of valid passports or national identity documents of each natural-person UBO and each designated director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport authority, or notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) and sworn Spanish translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC), arts. 20, 21, 22, 23, 31, 33; Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 174-177
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certificate) and Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio social (definitive registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) and its inscription in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an SL, minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; contribution must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution, with no separate escrow account mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, having resolved to incorporate a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under the LSC, hereby: (a) approve the draft articles of association and, if applicable, the valuation of non-cash contributions; (b) subscribe and fully pay up the entire share capital of EUR [amount], as allocated in the attached schedule; (c) designate the registered office at [address], Spain; (d) appoint [Name] as Sole Administrator and [Name] as Secretary; (e) authorise the notary to execute the public deed and authorise the appointed officers to apply for the provisional tax ID, register with the Mercantile Registry and complete all ancillary formalities, with authority to release the capital deposit certificate after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online via CIRCE/SUMATA portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) listing up to five preferred corporate names. The certificate confirms that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company and is valid for three months.
required_dossiers: DNI/NIE/passport of each incorporator or legal representative
Power of attorney if acting through a representative
Completed application form for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the proposed name, file an amended application with alternative names within two business days; the certificate is reissued without additional substantive review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Bank Account and Making the Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution chosen by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary formation account in a Spanish bank in the name of the company being incorporated. Transfer at least the full minimum share capital (EUR 3,000) into the account and obtain an official capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) specifying the depositor, account number, and amount, valid for the notarial deed signing.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Draft articles of association
Identity documents (NIE/passport) of each shareholder
Tax identification numbers of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate contains any discrepancy, request a corrected certificate from the bank before proceeding to the notary; any shortage or delay is cured by re-deposit and reissue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (notaría located in the province of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholder(s), including at least one incorporator, and the appointed officers must appear before the notary. The notary will incorporate the name certificate, bank capital deposit certificate, the approved by-laws, officer acceptance declarations, and any independent valuation of non-cash contributions. The notary verifies legal capacity and legal conformity of the deed, then signs and issues the first and second notarial copies.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate
Draft by-laws (estatutos sociales) and preliminary deed draft
NIE/TIE and passport of each shareholder and officer
Payment receipt or proof of notarial fees
Valuation report for non-cash contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises any formal defects, the parties execute a corrective rectification deed or amend the original deed; if the by-laws contain unlawful clauses, incorporate the notary's required adjustments and re-sign before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment and Filing of Transfer Tax and Capital Duties (ITPAJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT – Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), territorial delegation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 429 (Modalidad Operaciones Societarias de ITPAJD) within one month from the notarial deed execution. Calculate the tax based on the registered capital amount; in most newly incorporated SLs the effective rate is zero (0%) under the applicable exemption, but a tax return must still be filed for stamping on the deed copy for the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarised public deed
Tax identification data of shareholders
Self-declared assessment form (Form 429)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an incorrect exemption or assessment is identified, submit a rectification (autoliquidación complementaria) and, if necessary, apply for a refund within the four-year limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil de la provincia) corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first notarial deed copy and the payment evidence of ITPAJD to the Registry. The registrar verifies legal capacity of the parties, compliance with the LSC, and legality of the by-laws. Once approved, the company is registered and an official certificate of registration is issued.
required_dossiers: First copy of public deed
Evidence of ITPAJD filing and payment (Form 429 stamp)
Notarial fee and registry fee receipts
Name certificate and any prior supplementary notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends the registration, comply with the stated defect in a notarial or administrative rectification letter; if materially impossible, execute an amended deed and re-present within the calendar period allowed by the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Final Tax ID (NIF) and Starting Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (State Tax Administration Agency) – Central or territorial office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Mercantile Registry notifies AEAT electronically. The legal representative then obtains the final tax identification number (NIF) by presenting the registry certificate and deed. The company must also register for corporate tax, VAT, and any relevant local economic activity tax before issuing invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Mercantile Registry
Notarised public deed and statue copy
Identity document and NIE of the legal representative
Form 036/037 if self-registration is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIF is not automatically issued, file Form 036/037 directly at the AEAT office with the registration certificate; if the AEAT requires additional verification, provide the deed and by-laws and re-submit within the statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo and Consejería de Industria of the Autonomous Community where the plant operates
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad de Establecimiento Industrial / Inscripción en el Registro Industrial (Real Decreto 475/2007)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico; regional Consejería de Medio Ambiente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Category A / Annex I) if the manufacturing process includes galvanisation, surface treatment or thermal treatment of metals; otherwise Category B Registration under Ley 21/2013
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater limits: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, oils and greases ≤ 15 mg/L, total metals within the applicable EU BAT-AELs; VOC emissions ≤ 20 mg/Nm3 at source; hazardous waste tracking per Regulation (EC) 1013/2006 and storage segregation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) issued by the local authorities or an authorised body; structural load inspection certificate for the industrial building; occupational risk prevention clearance under Ley 31/1995, covering high-voltage electrical risks, cable-manufacturing machinery safety, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official portal: www.agenciatributaria.es; electronic taxpayer office: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident supplier: apply for a NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) with an 'N' identifier prefix via AEAT Form 036/037 (Censo de Empresarios), appointing a fiscal representative where IVA liability arises; a domestic ES_SL obtains a provisional NIF from the Central Mercantile Registry before incorporation, then files Form 036/037 and receives the definitive NIF after notarized deed execution and inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: a tax-resident Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is taxed on worldwide income at the standard corporate rate of 25% (reduced 15% for newly created entities with qualifying activity); a non-resident entity or branch without Spanish residency is taxed only on Spanish-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective hybrid classification exists; Spanish corporate law mandates entity-level taxation for SLs. Available statutory elections include: tax consolidation group regime (Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades Art. 103, subject to AEAT pre-approval); ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) holding-regime election; 15% reduced CIT for the first two profitable tax periods; patent box exemption (30% of qualifying income); R&D tax credit options; cash-basis VAT for eligible SMEs with turnover ≤ EUR 2,000,000; optional simplified VAT regimes for small businesses. Hybrid mismatch disallowances apply mandatorily under ATAD transposition, with no elective avoidance mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) — Spanish VAT/GST system harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold for persons established in Spain: any economic activity triggers mandatory IVA registration from the first euro of taxable turnover. EU-established distance sellers have a EUR 35,000 annual distance-selling threshold (general IT systems). Non-EU suppliers are required to register for IVA from the first euro of Spanish turnover, irrespective of any threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal transmission applies via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA): businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04, or in a VAT group, must submit invoice records to AEAT through web services within 4 business days (8 calendar days maximum). B2G invoices must use the Facturae format with digital signature. The Veri*factu regime (Royal Decree 1007/2023) will require certified invoicing software generating a QR-code hash and transmitting invoice integrity data to AEAT for all B2B transactions; no physical tax stamping is required, but digital clearance and traceability are compulsory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% export VAT rate (exemption with credit) applies under LIVA Art. 21 to tangible goods dispatched or transported by the seller or on the seller's account from Spanish territory to a destination outside the European Union, provided departure from the EU is evidenced by customs documentation and the goods leave the EU within 3 months from delivery; offshore services rendered to non-EU customers fall outside the scope of Spanish IVA under B2B place-of-supply rules, thereby achieving effective 0% taxation without formal zero-rating proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) with customs-validated exit stamp for consignment leaving the EU
Bill of Lading (or airway bill / CMR) showing the port or airport of discharge outside the European Union and consignee located outside Spain
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 proof evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the statutory repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT applies strict documentary scrutiny to export zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate physical departure or receipt of payment within 180 days triggers retrospective IVA assessment at 21% plus late-payment interest (interés de demora). Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the tax loss for material or negligent infractions (Ley General Tributaria Arts. 191-193), with specific SII transmission penalties of up to EUR 2,000 per record. The 4-year limitation period empowers AEAT to reopen historically claimed zero-rated exports. Fraudulent schemes exceeding EUR 120,000 constitute a criminal tax offense under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code, exposing management to imprisonment and disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks and under the regulatory framework of the European Central Bank (ECB), the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, and the Dirección General de Operaciones de Mercado. The Foreign Exchange regulatory perimeter is governed by EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and, in Spain, by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 on payment services and the Banco de España Circular regulating balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. No prior foreign exchange authorization is required for conversion of EUR into foreign currency, for profit remittance to non-resident shareholders, or for repatriation of capital from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). The only obligations are ex-post statistical declaration to Banco de España for transactions exceeding relevant thresholds (e.g., EUR 50,000 for most external payment operations and EUR 10,000 for cash transactions involving non-residents), and compliance with corporate income tax and non-resident dividend withholding tax rules. Profit remittances are permitted without foreign-exchange controls, but may be subject to Spanish tax withholding (typically 19% under domestic law, reduced under an applicable tax treaty) provided that the beneficiary submits the appropriate tax residence certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender, forced conversion, or minimum repatriation holding periods. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency abroad or in Spanish banks without mandatory conversion. However, for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, exporters must report transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 to Banco de España (form EI-04). The governing rule is that all export proceeds must be legally declared and booked in EUR at the applicable exchange rate under Spanish accounting standards, but there is no statutory timeline for conversion or surrender.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multicurrency Account / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account / Export Collection Account / Letter of Credit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with regulatory constraints. Spanish or EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating under PSD2 may offer cross-border EUR payment accounts and provide faster clearing via SEPA/SWIFT rails. However, for the ISIC 2732 subsea cable manufacturing business—which requires large-capacity escrow, trade finance (documentary letters of credit), and high-value export settlements—EMIs are viable only as supplementary collection/disbursement channels, not as primary treasury accounts. Offshore, non-EEA EMIs cannot legally provide payment services to a Spanish entity on a cross-border basis without a proper license or passport, and use of such rails would create AML/CFT compliance defects. The recommended structure is a Tier-1 Spanish bank as the principal account, with an optional EEA-licensed EMI for secondary euro collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not statutorily mandatory, but most Tier-1 Spanish banks require physical or video-identification KYC interviews for UBOs and directors, especially for a newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders. Remote opening is possible but generally only for EEA-resident UBOs or where a notarized power-of-attorney is granted to a Spanish resident legal representative. For a non-resident-owned SL in the export/manufacturing sector, Spanish banks commonly require an in-person meeting with the UBO or director (or the appointed representative) at the bank's Spanish branch, or a remote notarized interview, to satisfy the bank's AML/KYC risk appetite and the legal obligations under Law 10/2010 (Spanish AML Law). Expect a hybrid protocol: documentary submission remotely plus a physical signatory/KYC interview at the Spanish branch or a Spanish consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with UBOs residing in jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or tax-haven
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate structure chart; certificate of incorporation of the Spanish SL (escritura de constitución) and updated NIF certificate; passport copies of all UBOs with a notarized translation; proof of source of funds for initial capital; audited financial statements or equivalent of the parent entity; and a declaration of economic substance describing the Spanish manufacturing facilities, local plant capacity, and export operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value wire transfer activity inconsistent with expected transaction profile of a manufacturing company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed commercial contracts and pro-forma invoices for the subsea fiber-optic cable project; export licenses or permits (if applicable); a cash-flow forecast; bills of lading or shipping documents; and evidence of compliance with Spanish export control regulations for dual-use telecom infrastructure items.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of foreign-management signatories or absence of any locally resident officer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a valid power-of-attorney (poder notarial) granted to a Spanish resident representative, registered with the Commercial Registry; certified copy of the notarial deed; and the representative's NIF (DNI/NIE) and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business sector classification (subsea cable manufacturing) flagged for potential dual-use or national-security implications
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the company's CNAE code (2732 for manufacture of other electronic and electric wires and cables); product technical specifications confirming non-defense use; a signed declaration that the company is not subject to defense procurement or export restrictions unless licensed; and engagement with the Spanish Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be in EUR or convertible foreign currency via SWIFT MT103 or high-value SEPA payment, using the appropriate purpose code (e.g., 'EQUI' for equity injection or 'INVS' for direct investment). The remitting bank must include the Spanish SL's IBAN and the corporate name exactly as registered. The Spanish receiving bank will require proof of the equity subscription (notarized deed of increase in share capital), registration in the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil), and a statement to Banco de España (Declaración de Operaciones de Comercio Exterior / Investment Code). For amounts exceeding EUR 50,000, the bank typically requires an EI-04 declaration. The funds may be routed to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account and then released to the operating account only upon documentary verification of the capital increase and UBO 's registration in the Spanish Registro de Titularidades Reales.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements from the Spanish SL to suppliers, contractors, and overseas buyers include: (1) SWIFT MT103 messages for wire transfers in EUR or USD; (2) documentary letters of credit (ISIC 2732 equipment imports/exports) under ICC UCP 600; and (3) SEPA direct debit/credit in EUR for domestic and EU payments. Where the SL receives export settlement through a commercial LC, the advising/confirming bank located in Spain will credit the operational account upon presentation of compliant shipping documents. For urgent high-value bulk payments, the Spanish bank's online corporate channel may initiate SWIFT MT103 payments with pre-agreed fee/foreign-exchange arrangements. Compliance with Banco de España reporting thresholds and underlying commercial contracts is mandatory, and the bank may require declaration code (e.g., EI-04) for each cross-border transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts for EUR/USD or EUR/GBP settlement of commercial trade flows
FX swaps for managing temporary treasury liquidity mismatches across EUR/USD positions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) if the company holds long-term foreign currency debt or receivables, subject to EMIR clearing/reporting and bank's internal derivatives policy
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies where delivery is restricted (e.g., Latin American currencies such as BRL, MXN, or CLP, if applicable to project counterparties)

FX options (plain European-style options) for hedging firm export receivables, normally permitted only where the manufacturing SL has an underlying transactional exposure and the bank confirms suitability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval and filing, including beneficial ownership statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors prepare within 3 months after financial year-end; shareholders approve within 6 months; file within 1 month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, filing is generally due by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may be imposed after 1 year from the filing deadline. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies. Late filing alone does not automatically cause strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, late-payment interest, and collection surcharges apply. Unpaid tax may enter enforced collection, with additional enforcement costs and potential tax audits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and change notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales), as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information must be kept current. The annual beneficial ownership declaration is submitted with the annual accounts, and changes must be reported through the applicable registry or notarial process without undue delay.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry filing defects, registry closure, potential administrative penalties, and enhanced anti-money-laundering compliance scrutiny. False or incomplete information may create director and beneficial-owner liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements and profit allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; resolutions may be notarized or registered where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability for losses, shareholder challenge risk, and inability to complete timely annual accounts filing. The Commercial Registry may close the company's filing sheet for related non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of these limits for two consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average employees above 50. Audit may also be mandatory for regulated activities, securities offerings, certain grants or subsidies, consolidation obligations, or other statutory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) and applicable Spanish accounting regulations. IFRS is generally relevant to listed groups and permitted or required in specified consolidated-account contexts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owners. The annual accounts filing includes a beneficial ownership statement or confirmation. Any change in direct or indirect ownership or control must be reflected in the company's records and reported through the applicable notarial or registry channel.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and their powers
Annual accounts and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 650-1,650 annually, depending on city, address services, mail handling, and corporate secretarial scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000-7,500 for a non-complex small or medium-sized SL; materially higher for regulated, consolidated, or operationally complex businesses

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Temporary 23% rate for small businesses (turnover ≤ €1 million); R&D and innovation tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) via AEAT electronic portal (Cl@ve or digital certificate)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after exempt income, deductions, and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents declare only Spanish-source income; claim DTA relief via TRC submission

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before corporate tax application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign income generally exempt unless permanent establishment exists

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fines €600–€60,000 for late filing; daily surcharges €60–€600; criminal sanctions for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) from Spanish Tax Authorities and submit to withholding agent prior to dividend payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory (treaty rates 5–10%); Interest: 19% statutory (treaty rates 0% for related parties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applies to IP holding, finance, leasing, and administration; not triggered by manufacturing of subsea telecommunication fiber cables

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Modelo 100 by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines €600–€60,000 plus interest; possible criminal proceedings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil liability for tax debts, management disqualification, and imprisonment in aggravated cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transactions with related parties lacking arm's length documentation or applying non-compliant methods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, penalties up to 100% of additional tax, and criminal fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil, restitution orders, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaration of dividends, royalties, or interest to avoid WHT or shift profits without substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and asset confiscation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate roles, and prison sentences
